# Playtester

Discover and join alphas, betas, playtests, and demos for upcoming games.

## Recent Games

### [Necro Pop](https://playtester.io/necro-pop.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Necro Pop is an all-new action genre platformer we lovingly refer to as Arcadevania. On your adventure, you will discover new abilities, upgrades, secrets. You can free your ghostly friends using multiple combat abilities, magics, and maybe even a minion across multiple re-playable dungeons!  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Action, RPG, Arcade, Platformer, Puzzle, Dungeon Crawler, Hack and Slash, Metroidvania, Cute, Dark Fantasy, Dark Humor

### [HR.SOS](https://playtester.io/hrsos.md)
**Type:** Demo  
The company is falling apart, and you're both the HR cleaning up the mess and the CEO profiting from it. Optimize people, rebuild workflows, automate production, and watch the numbers go up.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Simulation, Strategy, Puzzle, Time Management, Idler, Resource Management, Economy, Automation, Sandbox, Management, Dark Humor, Third-Person, Capitalism, Retro

### [Radia Island](https://playtester.io/radia-island.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Radia Island is a civilization-building survival game. Lead your people to a new land, establish your first town, gather resources, research technologies, advance into the industrial age, and ultimately complete the space program.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Simulation, Strategy, City Builder, Colony Sim, Resource Management, Survival, Management, Sandbox, Building, Base Building, 4X, Economy, Automation

### [Dino Domino](https://playtester.io/dino-domino.md)
**Type:** Beta  
A pixel-art puzzle game where you can rewrite the rules! Swap commands to create: healing from traps, Medusa petrification, infinite fireball loops?! Play as an adorable little dinosaur🦖 on a mind-bending adventure to save the world!  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Puzzle, Cute, Turn-Based, Sokoban, Funny, Difficult, Board Game, Automation, Strategy

### [Calico Wilder and the Crystal Blade](https://playtester.io/calico-wilder-and-the-crystal-blade.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Calico Wilder and the Crystal Blade is a 3D platformer inspired by classics of the early 2000's. Join Relic Hunters Calico and Lilly as they traverse an ancient temple in search of a strange and powerful artifact: the Crystal Blade!  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Action, Adventure, Platformer, Cute, Third-Person, Funny, Fantasy, Magic, Comedy, Romance, Exploration

### [Ever After Again: A Stories Adventure](https://playtester.io/ever-after-again-a-stories-adventure.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Return to the world of Stories, or enter it for the first time, in an action RPG where your choices shape the adventure, a sarcastic narrator follows your every triumph and disaster, and you'll combine swords, sorcery, and flexible card-based powers to find the hero's path that will save the world!  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Action, Adventure, RPG, ARPG, Choices Matter, Multiple Endings, Story, Funny, Hack and Slash, Fantasy, Magic

### [Hellwire](https://playtester.io/hellwire.md)
**Type:** Demo  
A dueling deckbuilder game against other players. Learn the rules of the bizarre match unfolding before you, turn the tide with clever (and not so clever) abilities, don’t get tangled in the wires, and pray for the mercy of the Biomechanical Goat.  
**Categories:** Multiplayer, PvP, Strategy, Turn-Based, First-Person, Tabletop, Card Game, Atmospheric

### [Torizon Telecom](https://playtester.io/torizon-telecom.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Torizon Telecom is a text-based FPS game set in a vast world composed entirely of text. “Telecom”—a world where everything is text. “Telecom”... But does any other world exist beyond “Telecom”...? Or is “Telecom” the only one that exists...?  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Action, Adventure, FPS, Text-Based, First-Person, Shooter, Boomer Shooter, Difficult, Cyberpunk

### [Spooky Ride](https://playtester.io/spooky-ride.md)
**Type:** Beta  
Team up with friends to navigate treacherous trials on bikes while carrying a demanding passenger who literally holds the world together. Keep Little Foot happy and calm to survive the madness, or prepare to watch your friendship (and the universe) fall apart in spectacular fashion.  
**Categories:** Multiplayer, Online Co-op, Adventure, Racing, Co-op, Funny, Comedy, Physics, Mystery, Horror, Psychological Horror, Atmospheric, Action, Puzzle, Platformer, Cute

### [Lo and Behold](https://playtester.io/lo-and-behold.md)
**Type:** Beta  
Lo and Behold is a cozy tinged roguelike where you fight to protect a quirky village of animal folk. Venture out to fight corrupted beasts, use elemental powers to shape your own spells, and return with resources to rebuild and flourish Behold Village into a lively, magical home.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Action, Adventure, Roguelike, Base Building, Cute, Dungeon Crawler, Hack and Slash, Fantasy, Cozy

### [Truck World: Australia](https://playtester.io/truck-world-australia.md)
**Type:** Beta  
Take a breathtaking journey across Australia behind the wheel of a multi-ton truck. Explore highways and dirt tracks, enjoy the beautiful nature. Step out of the cab to manually secure the hitch and inspect your cargo. Freedom and realism await you!  
**Categories:** Adventure, Racing, Simulation, Driving, Open World, Exploration, Economy, Multiplayer, Management, Atmospheric, Third-Person, First-Person

### [Wild West Pioneers](https://playtester.io/wild-west-pioneers.md)
**Type:** Beta  
Wild West Pioneers is a city-builder adventure about leading settlers into the untamed frontier. Build and manage growing settlements, establish production chains, and explore the world. Follow a story of gold rush dreams, dangerous encounters, and the search for your family.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Simulation, Strategy, City Builder, Colony Sim, Sandbox, Exploration, Atmospheric, 4X, Building, Economy, Base Building, Survival, Historical, Management, Resource Management

### [Deadpact](https://playtester.io/deadpact.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Sentenced to death, you're sent into the dark for one last chance at freedom. The things hunting you are not mindless monsters. Each one hunts you, learns your every move, and never forgets. Outsmart them, or die. Every choice you make changes how your story ends.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Adventure, Survival Horror, Story, Dungeon Crawler, Medieval, Exploration, Horror, First-Person, Atmospheric, Thriller, Stealth, Multiple Endings

### [Harbourlight](https://playtester.io/harbourlight.md)
**Type:** Beta  
Warm light, late nights, one guest at a time. Grow, raise and catch your ingredients, then build each dish by hand across eight flavours, tailored to whoever's at the counter. Listen as your regulars open up, and watch a sleepy harbour town wake up as new faces arrive with new tastes to learn.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Simulation, Farming Sim, Cooking, Life Sim, Cozy, Wholesome, Story, Cute, Atmospheric, Fishing, Romance

### [Maid Supremacy: Achieving World Domination with a Tank!](https://playtester.io/maid-supremacy-achieving-world-domination-with-a-tank.md)
**Type:** Demo  
A 3D action-shooter campaign about maids controlling a drifting tank with multiple weapon extensions! Destroy those filthy uncultured girls and prove that MAIDS ARE BETTER, alone or with your friends! Personalize your tank and unlock even more parts!  
**Categories:** Multiplayer, Online Co-op, Action, Adventure, Shooter, Shoot 'Em Up, Third-Person Shooter, Anime, Third-Person, Military, War, Female Protagonist, PvE, Score Attack

### [Warband](https://playtester.io/warband.md)
**Type:** Beta  
Warband is a wave-crusher, boss-rusher and mystery-busting roguelite. Choose your commander, recruit for your warband and stock up at the shop to create unique combinations every run whilst fighting off waves of enemies and bosses a plenty. Can you turn the tide and get Thornhallow back on its feet?  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, Action, Adventure, Strategy, Boss Rush, Bullet Heaven, Bullet Hell, Medieval, Dark Fantasy, Atmospheric, Inventory Management, Roguelike

### [No Brakes Club](https://playtester.io/no-brakes-club.md)
**Type:** Beta  
A retro multiplayer platformer for up to 10 players per round. Sprint, sabotage, and backstab your way through quickfire minigames where every round takes seconds to learn and one mistake to lose.  
**Categories:** Multiplayer, PvP, Racing, Battle Royale, Platformer, Party Game, Cute, Physics, Retro, MMO

### [Shrike](https://playtester.io/shrike.md)
**Type:** Demo  
Pickpocket rival birds to build a deck. A turn-based roguelike deckbuilder about a tiny bird's grim migration north through a wretched medieval kingdom. Steal abilities, chart your migratory route, survive.  
**Categories:** Singleplayer, RPG, Strategy, Roguelike, Deckbuilder, Turn-Based, Card Battler, Card Game, Dungeon Crawler, Medieval, Dark

### [Fading Light](https://playtester.io/fading-light.md)
**Type:** Beta  
In a world of eternal darkness, navigate the unknown with only the glow of your companion, Spark. Craft arrows from the environment to survive, uncover lost secrets of an ancient world, and push forward through the shadows into hope. Will you find your way, or will the dark consume you?  
**Categories:** Multiplayer, Action, Adventure, Metroidvania, Platformer, Cute, Puzzle, Atmospheric, Difficult, Soulslike, Survival, Story, Co-op, Dark

### [Unwell](https://playtester.io/unwell.md)

# Frequently Asked Questions

## What is Playtester?
Playtester is a platform where you can discover and join alphas, betas, playtests, and demos for upcoming games across Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, and more.

## Is Playtester affiliated with Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, or other platforms?
No. Playtester operates independently and isn’t affiliated with Valve Corporation, Sony Interactive Entertainment, Microsoft Corporation, Nintendo, or any other platform holders. All logos and trademarks are the property of their respective owners.

## How do I join playtests?
Simply browse the games listed on Playtester. Each page includes instructions or links to the relevant store, such as Steam or console storefronts, so you can sign up or download the playtest directly from the official source.

## I’m a developer. How can I add my game to Playtester?
Click "Add a Game" in the navigation menu and fill out the submission form. Once we review and approve your game, it will appear in our listings for players to discover.

## What types of games are allowed on Playtester?
We accept a wide variety of games but DO NOT list any containing NSFW content (e.g., sexual content, nudity, hentai), NFT/crypto-based games, asset flips, or titles restricted to proprietary storefronts or closed ecosystems (e.g., Roblox experiences, Fortnite engine projects). This helps keep our platform accessible, trustworthy, and compliant for everyone.

## How can I connect with developers or the community?
Join the official [Playtester Discord](https://discord.gg/playtesterhq). Many developers and fellow players are active there, so you can share feedback, ask questions, and get to know the community.

Visit [playtester.io/faqs](https://playtester.io/faqs) for more frequently asked questions.

<!-- end of /faqs -->

# Community Guidelines

Explore the community guidelines that help maintain a safe and positive space on Playtester.

## Be Respectful
Treat all community members with respect and kindness.

## No Spam
Don’t post repetitive content or promotional material without permission.

## Stay On Topic
Keep discussions related to game testing and feedback.

## Report Issues
If you encounter problems with a game listing, use the report feature.

## Support Developers
Provide constructive feedback to help improve the games you test.

## Follow Platform Rules
Respect the terms of service of the platforms where games are hosted (Steam, PlayStation, Xbox, etc.).

## No Piracy
Only share and discuss legitimate, officially available playtests.

Visit [playtester.io/guidelines](https://playtester.io/guidelines) for the complete community guidelines.

Last updated: February 26, 2026

Playtester allows users to discover and join game playtests across various platforms. By accessing or using our platform, you agree to these terms.

## 2. Account Creation
You can create an account using your email or by logging in with Discord or Steam. You must be at least 13 years old to use Playtester.

## 3. Data and Privacy
We collect certain information to provide our services, as described in our Privacy Policy. We use cookies to enhance your experience.

## 4. Using the Platform
When using Playtester, you agree not to:
- Use the platform for any illegal activities
- Interfere with the platform’s operation or security
- Post harmful or offensive content

## 5. User Content
You may post comments or feedback on games. You own your content but allow us to use it to improve the platform.

## 6. Third-Party Links
We may include links to game store pages. We aren’t responsible for the content or privacy practices of those third-party sites.

## 7. Account Termination
You can delete your account anytime by contacting us. We may suspend or terminate your access if you violate these terms.

## 8. Disclaimers
Playtester is provided "as is." We can’t guarantee it will always be available or error-free.

## 9. Contact Us
Have questions? Reach out to us at contact@playtester.io

# Privacy Policy

Last updated: February 26, 2026

## 1. Introduction
This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your data when you interact with Playtester.

## 2. Information We Collect
- **Personal Information:** Email address, username, OAuth data from Discord and Steam
- **Non-Personal Information:** Interaction data, cookies for preferences

## 3. How We Use Your Information
- Account management and authentication
- Platform functionality and game recommendations
- Analytics to improve our platform
- Communication about updates and changes

## 4. How We Share Your Information
We do not sell your personal information. We may share data with:
- Third-party OAuth providers (Discord, Steam)
- Service providers (Vercel for hosting)
- Legal authorities when required by law

## 5. Cookies and Similar Technologies
We use cookies to remember login sessions, understand interactions, and analyze trends.

## 6. Data Security
We use industry-standard security measures to safeguard your personal information.

## 7. Data Retention
We retain data only as long as necessary. Account deletion removes data within 30 days.

## 8. Your Rights
You have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your data.

## 9. Children’s Privacy
Playtester is not intended for children under 13.

## 10. Contact Information
Email: contact@playtester.io

For the full privacy policy, visit [playtester.io/privacy](https://playtester.io/privacy).

# Search

## Search Tips
- Use keywords like "horror", "multiplayer", "roguelike"
- Filter by platform: Steam, PlayStation, Xbox, Epic Games, etc.
- Filter by type: Alpha, Beta, Demo, Playtest
- Browse by categories for genre-specific games

# Acknowledgements

Playtester is built on the shoulders of giants, with deep gratitude for the open-source community that empowers our vision.

## Open Source Libraries

We are grateful to the creators and maintainers of the countless open-source packages that form the foundation of our platform.

## Key Technologies
- **Next.js** - React framework for production
- **Tailwind CSS** - Utility-first CSS framework
- **ShadCN UI** - Reusable components built with Radix UI and Tailwind
- **Supabase** - Open source Firebase alternative for database and authentication
- **Vercel** - Platform for deploying and hosting
- **React Query** - Data fetching and state management
- **Phosphor Icons** - Flexible icon family

## Contributors
Thanks to everyone who has contributed to making Playtester better through feedback, bug reports, and suggestions.

## License Compliance
We’re committed to complying with all licenses. For detailed license information, visit [playtester.io/licenses](https://playtester.io/licenses)

## Blog posts

# How we review and curate games at Playtester

By Shaan Shivanandan · April 18, 2026

#Platform

Every game on Playtester is reviewed before it is listed. There is no automated pipeline, and no open submission queue that publishes on its own. A small team looks at the build, the store page, the trailer, and the assets, and decides whether the game fits the platform. We see between fifty and a hundred submissions a week, and roughly a third end up listed. This post explains how that decision is made and what it is designed to protect.

![An angled grid of game capsules shown in varying art styles, reflecting the range of titles reviewed for Playtester.](https://cdn.playtester.io/blog/how-we-review-and-curate-games-at-playtester/images/game-covers-grid.webp?t=1776548654641 "Game capsules across styles")

## What makes a game a good fit
A capsule that reads clearly at small sizes, because that is where most players will see it first. A trailer that runs smoothly and shows the actual game. A store page with metadata that is accurate and descriptions written with care. A Steam depot history that reflects ongoing development, not a build that has been sitting unchanged for months. A team that is reachable and engaged, whether through direct submission, social presence, or devlogs.

These are the signals we look for, and none of them are unusual. Most developers who take their launch seriously already meet them. When they come together, a game is usually a straightforward yes.

## What we do not list
A few categories sit outside the scope of the platform. Crypto and NFT games. Games whose entire premise is explicit sexual content. Games that have already released. Games without a Steam page, a playable demo or active playtest, or an English option for dialogue or subtitles. Mature themes are fine when they are part of a larger work.

Our approach to AI-generated content is measured rather than absolute. Auxiliary uses in non-essential places are generally acceptable. For the surfaces a player uses to recognize a game (capsules, logos, and key art) we expect the work to come from the team behind it. Those first impressions carry too much weight to be left to anything else.

## How a listing is built
Developers do not publish listings on Playtester. We build them. Once a game clears review, we standardize the metadata, choose and order the media, write a clean short description, and verify that every link works. The structure has to be consistent across thousands of games for browsing to feel calm rather than noisy.

![A Playtester game detail page shown on a desktop monitor, with the video player, metadata column, and media thumbnails visible.](https://cdn.playtester.io/blog/how-we-review-and-curate-games-at-playtester/images/game-review-screen.webp?t=1776548698075 "Playtester game listing page")

This is the slowest part of the process and the part most platforms skip. It is also the part players feel most directly, even if they never think about it.

## Why curation is the product
There are faster ways to run a discovery platform. Open submissions, automated ingestion, and engagement-driven ranking would all let us list more games with less effort. They would also produce a different kind of feed, larger, louder, and harder to trust.

When a player opens Playtester, the implicit promise is that someone has already done the work of looking. Every game on the page is there because it earned a spot, and the bar is the reason the platform is worth returning to. Curation is not a finishing layer on top of discovery. It is the product.

Source: https://playtester.io/blog/how-we-review-and-curate-games-at-playtester

<!-- end of /blog/how-we-review-and-curate-games-at-playtester -->

# Introducing Playtester

By Shaan Shivanandan · February 22, 2026

#Platform

Game discovery today is fragmented. Players looking for alphas, betas, and demos are forced to jump between Reddit threads, Discord servers, itch.io pages, Steam events, SteamDB, and social feeds across multiple platforms. There is no single place to reliably see what is playable now or what is opening next. As a result, meaningful playtests are easy to miss, and many players only discover games after the opportunity to try them has already passed.

![Mobile views of Reddit, Bluesky, and itch.io showing game demo posts across separate platforms.](https://cdn.playtester.io/blog/introducing-playtester/images/playtester-app-preview.webp?t=1771771944853 "Fragmented game discovery across platforms")

Playtester was created to make pre-release discovery easier and more inclusive. It is a curated place to discover upcoming games, including alphas, betas, demos, and early access builds, presented in a single, continuously updated feed. The goal is to help players stay informed and give developers a clearer path to visibility during the most fragile stage of development.

## Background

Most existing discovery platforms are built around released titles. Playtester takes a different approach by focusing entirely on pre-release games. When a playtest ends or a game ships, it is deprioritized. What remains is a live view of what players can actually access now, rather than an archive of stale listings. This keeps the feed relevant and ensures that discovery reflects the present.

Every game on Playtester is manually curated. Games may be submitted by developers or surfaced through discovery, but inclusion is intentional. We avoid adult-only content, crypto projects, AI asset flips, and anything that does not respect players’ time. The aim is not to list everything, but to surface the strongest upcoming experiences and maintain a quality bar across the platform.

Playtester is designed to serve both players and developers. It began as a tool for players who wanted a better way to find demos, and naturally evolved into a discovery channel for developers seeking exposure. Visibility should not be a luxury, and discovering a major playtest should not depend on being in the right Discord server at the right time. Players deserve to know what is available, and developers deserve a place where early work can be found without noise.

![Three dark stat cards show 1M players reached, 150K monthly views, and 193 countries reached.](https://cdn.playtester.io/blog/introducing-playtester/images/stats-dashboard.webp?t=1771924413254 "Playtester platform reach and global usage statistics")

Since launching in November 2024, Playtester has grown steadily. The platform has listed over 3,400 games and generated more than 1 million page views, with 150,000 monthly views from players across 193 countries. What began as a simple experiment has evolved into a space for pre-release game discovery.

## Looking ahead

Playtester will continue to focus on pre-release discovery while refining how players and developers interact during this phase. A near-term focus is enabling structured feedback, giving players a way to share insights directly with developers through the platform in a way that is useful and respectful.

Longer term, the goal is for Playtester to become the default place to discover alphas, betas, and demos, and a natural part of release roadmaps for studios of all sizes. Discovery should feel timely, reliable, and consistently worth returning to, whether you are an indie team testing your first build or a larger studio preparing a wider release.

![Playtester homepage showing a featured banner and a grid of playable pre-release games.](https://cdn.playtester.io/blog/introducing-playtester/images/playtester-homepage-screenshot.webp?t=1771762037932 "Playtester homepage feed")

Playtester is open to anyone who enjoys discovering games early. Browsing does not require an account, and the platform is designed to be something players come back to regularly.

You can start discovering at [playtester.io](https://playtester.io/), and follow updates at [@playtesterhq](https://x.com/playtesterhq) on X (Twitter).

Source: https://playtester.io/blog/introducing-playtester
